docs.text: Authentication The DriverApp API uses secure authentication mechanisms to validate users and sessions. 🔑 Authentication Tokens Access Tokens: Short-lived tokens required for API calls. Refresh Tokens: Used to obtain new access tokens securely. Tokens must be included in request headers to authenticate. 🔐 Session Management Sessions are tracked using unique SessionID . Each session is associated with a user and bundle. Expired sessions must be renewed via re-authentication. 🛡️ Security Best Practices Always use HTTPS for API requests. Store tokens securely on the client side. Revoke tokens on logout or suspected compromise. Validate tokens on each request. 📄 Example Authentication Flow User logs in with credentials. Server issues an access token and refresh token. Client includes access token in API calls. Upon expiry, client uses refresh token to get a new access token. ⚠️ Common Errors 401 Unauthorized: Invalid or expired token. 403 Forbidden: Token does not have permission for requested resource. 🔗 Further Integration Tips Implement token rotation to reduce risks. Monitor failed authentication attempts. Use scopes or roles within tokens for fine-grained access control. For detailed API authentication specs, refer to the API reference documentation.

docs.text: Overview This document provides a high-level summary of the DriverApp API and its key components. 🚗 What is DriverApp API? DriverApp API is a comprehensive backend service designed to manage drivers, trips, payments, and related logistics for ride-sharing or delivery platforms. 🌟 Key Features User Management: Register and manage drivers, riders, and admins. Trip Management: Create, update, and track trips in real-time. Payments: Handle payment processing, settlements, and refunds. Authentication & Security: Secure API access using token-based authentication. Webhooks: Real-time notifications for important events. 🗂️ Core Components Component Description Authentication User login and session management Users Management of driver and rider profiles Trips Scheduling and tracking trip details Payments Processing fares, commissions, and payouts Webhooks Event-driven updates and callbacks ⚙️ API Architecture RESTful endpoints using JSON payloads. Secure access via OAuth2 or API tokens. Support for asynchronous event notifications via webhooks. 🚀 Getting Started Obtain API credentials. Authenticate and acquire access tokens. Use API endpoints to manage users, trips, and payments. Set up webhooks to receive real-time updates. 📚 Documentation Structure Authentication: How to log in and manage sessions. Users: Driver and rider data models and operations. Trips: Creating and managing trips. Payments: Payment flows and reconciliation. Webhooks: Configuring event notifications. For detailed API specifications, please refer to the individual endpoint documentation.

docs.text: Payments The DriverApp API does not provide a direct "payments" endpoint. However, trip-related events and associated metadata can be used to drive payment calculations, reimbursements, or invoicing in external systems. This document explains how payment-relevant data can be extracted and utilized effectively. 📌 Payment Triggers Driver trip events act as indirect triggers for payments. The most relevant events for billing purposes include: Pickup and drop-off milestones Arrival and departure timestamps Mileage and location data Digital signatures and uploaded documents 🚚 Common Payment Scenarios 1. Completed Trip Billing Use the DO Stop Confirmation or DO Stop Departure events as indicators that a trip is complete and eligible for billing. 2. Mileage-Based Payments Extract the mileage data embedded in events to calculate distance-based compensation. 3. Proof-of-Delivery Attachments Leverage documents submitted with Signature Confirmation events as proof for compliance or billing validation. 💼 Example Data Points for Billing Field Description Example Mileage Total distance traveled 17074.1732 EventTime Timestamp of event 2022-05-24T06-31-19Z SignedBy Name of signer DOE, JOHN DocumentData Signature or image file ID file:d08efda3... 🧾 Sample Payment Event Flow Driver picks up the passenger Event: PU Stop Departure Driver drops off the passenger Event: DO Stop Arrival Signature is collected Event: DO Signature Confirmation Trip ends Event: DO Stop Departure 🔐 Security and Validation Ensure all payment-related data is transmitted over secure channels. Validate session tokens and bundle identifiers. Use event timestamps and signatures to audit and confirm payments. 🔗 Integration Ideas Sync events with your billing platform to generate invoices. Store digital signatures for dispute resolution. Calculate per-mile compensation dynamically using Mileage . 📬 Questions? For more information about integrating payment systems with DriverApp event data, contact the integration support team.

docs.text: Users This document describes the user-related data model and common operations for DriverApp users. 👥 User Types Drivers: Users who perform trips and deliveries. Riders: Passengers or recipients of trips. Admins: System administrators with elevated privileges. 📝 User Data Fields Field Description Example UserID Unique identifier user:abc123 UserName User’s display or login name jdoe Role User role (Driver, Rider, Admin) Driver ContactInfo Email or phone number john.doe@example.com Status Active, Inactive, Suspended Active 🔄 User Lifecycle Creation: Users registered via signup or import. Modification: Updates to user info or roles. Deactivation: Users can be deactivated without deletion. Deletion: Permanent removal of user data. 🔐 Security Considerations Passwords must be stored hashed and salted. Role-based access control (RBAC) governs permissions. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is recommended. 📌 Common User Operations Create a new user. Update user profile or permissions. Retrieve user details by ID. Deactivate or delete a user. 🔗 Integration Notes Sync user data with external identity providers. Audit user activity for compliance. Use unique user IDs consistently across systems. For API details on user management, see the user management API reference.

docs.text: Webhooks Webhooks provide a way for the DriverApp API to send real-time notifications to your system when specific events occur. 📬 What are Webhooks? Webhooks are HTTP callbacks triggered by events in the DriverApp system. They allow your application to react instantly to important changes without polling the API. 🔔 Supported Events Event Name Description trip.created A new trip has been created trip.updated A trip’s status or details have changed payment.completed A payment transaction has been successfully processed user.updated Changes to user profile or status session.expired User session has expired 🔧 Setting Up Webhooks Register your webhook URL: Provide a publicly accessible HTTPS endpoint. Subscribe to events: Specify which events you want to receive. Verify webhook requests: Use the provided signature header to ensure payload integrity. Handle incoming requests: Parse JSON payloads and update your system accordingly. 🔐 Security All webhook requests include a signature header to verify authenticity. Use HTTPS to encrypt webhook traffic. Validate incoming payloads before processing. 📦 Payload Structure Each webhook payload includes: event : The name of the event triggered. timestamp : When the event occurred. data : Event-specific information (e.g., trip details, payment info). Example: ```json { "event": "trip.created", "timestamp": "2025-08-19T12:34:56Z", "data": { "tripID": "trip:xyz789", "driverID": "user:abc123", "status": "scheduled", "pickupLocation": "123 Main St" } }
